children: Indian benchmark indices are likely to open on a strong note on September 3, tracking GIFT Nifty, which was trading higher at around 24,082.50 in early trade.

Indian equity indices ended weak on September 2, extended selling on the third consecutive day, amid a sharp surge in crude oil prices on the back of escalating geopolitical tensions in West Asia.

Amid weak global cues, the Indian equity indices opened lower and with extended selling Nifty tested day's low of 23,786.80, however, managed to close just above 23900 level after the closing auction session (CAS).
At close, the Sensex was down 373.93 points or 0.49 percent at 76,570.35, and the Nifty was down 141.35 points or 0.59 percent at 23,914.45.
The broader market also ended lower, with Nifty midcap index falling 0.5 percent and smallcap index falling 0.4 percent.
Here is how financial markets across the globe fared overnight:
GIFT Nifty (Up)
GIFT Nifty was trading with a gain of more than 100 points at around 24,082.50 in early trade, indicating a strong opening for the domestic equity markets.
Asian Equities (Up)
Asian stocks rose and oil snapped a three-day rally after President Donald Trump played down the prospect
of a prolonged conflict with Iran.
Gains in Japan and South Korea helped MSCI’s Asia Pacific equities gauge advance 0.4%, rebounding from a selloff on
Wednesday.
Technology shares drew attention after Broadcom Inc. predicted a boom in artificial intelligence chip sales over the
next two years.
US Equities (Gain)

Wall Street advanced on Wednesday, notching a partial rebound from a ​three-day losing streak as investors searched for deals among stocks and sectors that might have been oversold amid recent risk-off ‌moves.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 295.01 points, or 0.56%, to 53,061.89, the S&P ​500 gained 35.16 points, or 0.46%, to 7,666.63 and the Nasdaq Composite gained 118.05 points, or 0.45%, to 26,217.83.
Dollar Index (Down)
The dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies including the yen and the euro, was down marginally on Thursday.
US Bond Yield (Up)
The yield on 10-year Treasuries and 2-year Treasuries were little changed at 4.78% and 4.37%, respectively.
Asian currencies (Up)

Asian currencies were mostly stronger against the US dollar, with the Malaysian ringgit (+0.235%) and Thai baht (+0.118%) leading the gains. The Indonesian rupiah (-0.107%) was the only currency in the basket to weaken.
Crude (Down)
Oil prices edged lower on Thursday as investors weighed the uncertainty of renewed military strikes between the U.S. and Iran that risk disrupting supplies from the Middle East.
Gold (Jumps)
Gold advanced as the dollar pushed lower, with traders assessing remarks from policymakers that shed light on the Federal Reserve’s interest-rate path.
Fund Flow Action

Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) continued their buying for the second consecutive session on September 2, investing Rs 6,688 crore in Indian equities. Domestic institutional investors (DIIs) also remained supportive, pumping in Rs 2,812 crore during the session.
